<reason>B made the stronger comparative case: accountable access can preserve research and offline use while retaining obstacles to proliferation, without promising perfect containment. B also specified evidence that could justify release, answering A’s charge of permanent prohibition. A’s unfinished-test exception did not resolve credible hazards lacking reliable evaluations. Its closing repeated the assumption that attackers obtain withheld models while defenders remain excluded, despite B’s explicit research-access provision. A established genuine delay and competition costs, but B answered those better than A answered irreversible release under material uncertainty.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s second rebuttal distinguished unfinished tests from credible risks that cannot yet be reliably tested. This exposed the remaining gap in A’s demonstrated-threshold rule while directly rejecting A’s characterization of unresolved risks as merely unspecified dread.</best_rebuttal>
